relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: From 1956–1958, he studied at the University of Allahabad and obtained a B.A. in History, Philosophy and English literature.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: From 1958–1960 he studied at the University of Gorakhpur and obtained a M.A. in Ancient History of Culture

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: He had the privilege of studying Buddhism and Ancient Indian History under ProfessorGovind Chandra Pande. G. C. Pande played the decisive role in Joshi's formation as a Buddhist scholar. The former also supervised the latter's PhD thesis

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: In 1964 Joshi obtained his PhD from Gorakhpur University

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: and a second M.A. in Pali from Banaras Hindu University.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: L. M. Joshi held his first lecture post as Assistant Professor at the Department of Ancient History, Culture & Archaeology, University of Gorakhpur, from 1961–1967.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: In 1968 he was offered a senior research fellowship in the Department of Comparative Religion, Punjabi University, Patiala.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: from 1969–1970, he went to USA as postdoctoral visiting fellow in Comparative Religion at the Center for the Study of World Religions, Harvard University, Cambridge, Mass.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: There was where Prof. Joshi met his lifelong friend Robert Thurman, the well known Tibetologist

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: and Prof. Wilfred Cantwell Smith, who impressed him deeply and whom he often quoted later on

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: Back in India he was appointed Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at the Department of Religious Studies, Punjabi University, a post he held from 1971 to 1975.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.evidence: In 1976 the same university offered him a professorship until 1981.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.role: Henry R. Luce Visiting Professor of Comparative Religious Ethics
relations.evidence: first as Henry R. Luce Visiting Professor of Comparative Religious Ethics at Amherst College, Amherst, Massachusetts

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.role: Margaret Gest Visiting Professor of Comparative Religion
relations.evidence: and subsequently as Margaret Gest Visiting Professor of Comparative Religion at Haverford College, Pennsylvania.

relations.subject: Lal Mani Joshi
relations.object: Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies
relations.evidence: to engage in his new responsibilities as Research Professor of Buddhist Studies at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sarnath, in June 1984
